findings.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:62-92 — findFirst-then-create has no DB unique constraint on (userId, appId) backing it, so two concurrent webhook deliveries for the same user+app both miss the findFirst and both insert, producing duplicate Credential rows for the same app (confidence=75, severity=P1)

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:83-90 — credential is created with raw userId ownership and no team/org scoping check, an architectural mismatch with packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/createOAuthAppCredential.ts in the same diff which explicitly models team-owned credentials (teamId, throwIfNotHaveAdminAccessToTeam); the webhook path bypasses that ownership model entirely and only trusts appSlug->app existence, not user eligibility for the app (confidence=70, severity=P2)

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:5-11 — the computed property keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` both evaluate to the literal string "[object Object]" (default Object.prototype.toString on a ZodString/ZodOptional instance, not a dynamic field-name matcher), so minimumTokenResponseSchema collapses to effectively `{ access_token: z.string(), "[object Object]": z.unknown().optional() }" — it does not validate an expiry field or "any numeric property" as the comment claims, and any object with a string access_token passes for every one of the 5+ integrations routed through the sync path (confidence=95, severity=P1)

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:25-27 — when refresh_token is absent from the response, the function backfills the literal sentinel string "refresh_token" into the persisted credential key instead of preserving the prior refresh_token or erroring, corrupting credential.key so the next refresh attempt sends the garbage literal upstream as the OAuth refresh_token (confidence=90, severity=P1)

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:21-23 — parseRefreshTokenResponse now throws on any schema mismatch instead of returning a safeParse-shaped failure for the caller to handle gracefully, which changes every integration's refresh error-handling architecture from "log and continue with best-effort/stale token data" (the old office365 pattern of `tokenResponse.success && tokenResponse.data` spread) to "hard throw," and the `tokenResponse.success && tokenResponse.data` guard left in office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts is now dead code since a failed parse never returns to that line (confidence=65, severity=P1)

packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:243-267 — the console.error logging of zod validation failures on refresh was deleted with no replacement, so if a caller upstream ever catches the new thrown Error, the concrete validation diagnostics (what field failed, what the provider actually returned) are lost, removing the only observability into a wrong/incompatible sync-endpoint response for this integration (confidence=60, severity=P2)

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:5 — refresh routing is toggled by a single process-wide env pair (APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED + CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT) injected into every integration's refresh closure with no per-integration or per-credential opt-in, so a misconfigured or unreachable sync endpoint breaks token refresh for google, hubspot, lark, and office365 calendar/video simultaneously instead of failing one integration at a time (confidence=70, severity=P2)

packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:75-99 — salesforce's refresh path was NOT wired through refreshOAuthTokens (it always calls login.salesforce.com directly) yet it still calls parseRefreshTokenResponse, which switches to the broken minimumTokenResponseSchema whenever the global APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED+CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT flags are set even though salesforce never talks to the sync endpoint — an inconsistent integration boundary where turning on sync for other apps silently weakens salesforce's own-provider response validation too (confidence=65, severity=P2)

packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:74-97 — `getClient` posts directly to `https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token` instead of going through `refreshOAuthTokens`, so when APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED + CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, Salesforce's refresh silently bypasses the sync endpoint that googlecalendar/hubspot/larkcalendar/office365calendar/office365video/webex all honor, leaving Salesforce credentials never synced from the parent app while every other integration is (confidence=95, severity=P1).

packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:63-108 — `getClient` unconditionally calls the Salesforce token-refresh endpoint and does a `prisma.credential.update` on every `getClient` invocation (called from the constructor on every `new SalesforceCalendarService`), with no expiry check, unlike the migrated integrations whose `refreshAccessToken` is only invoked when the SDK/library detects an expired token, meaning Salesforce now refreshes (and syncs, once fixed) on every request instead of only when needed (confidence=60, severity=P2).

.env.example:242-245 — the comment states `CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY` "must be 32 bytes for AES256 encryption algorithm" but the accompanying example command is `openssl rand -base64 24`, which generates only 24 raw random bytes (base64-encoded to 32 characters, not 32 raw bytes); a self-hoster following the doc literally gets a 24-byte key, which will fail or misbehave against an AES-256 cipher expecting a 32-byte key (confidence=90, severity=P2).

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:31,57-59 — `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body)` and `symmetricDecrypt(reqBody.keys, ...)` / `JSON.parse(...)` are called with no try/catch, so a malformed body, wrong/missing encryption key, or non-JSON decrypted payload throws an unhandled exception yielding a generic 500 instead of a validated 4xx response, despite this endpoint accepting credential payloads from an external "parent application" (confidence=75, severity=P2).

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth (refreshOAuthTokens.ts, parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts) and apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts — zero test files exist anywhere in the diff for the new webhook route, refreshOAuthTokens wrapper, or parseRefreshTokenResponse validator, i.e. a credential-writing/security-sensitive feature ships with no automated verification of the sync-enabled vs sync-disabled code paths (confidence=90, severity=P2).

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/decodeOAuthState.ts:3 — `import type { IntegrationOAuthCallbackState } from "../../types"` resolves to packages/app-store/types, which does not exist anywhere in the repo (grep confirms zero definitions of IntegrationOAuthCallbackState), so this file and every one of its ~9 consumers (googlecalendar/hubspot/larkcalendar/office365calendar/office365video/salesforce/stripepayment/tandemvideo/webex callback.ts files) fail to compile (confidence=100, severity=P0)

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/encodeOAuthState.ts:3 — identical fabricated import `from "../../types"` for the non-existent `IntegrationOAuthCallbackState` type breaks this file and all its consumers (googlecalendar/hubspot/larkcalendar/office365calendar/office365video/salesforce/zoho-bigin add.ts files) (confidence=100, severity=P0)

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/createOAuthAppCredential.ts:7 — `import { throwIfNotHaveAdminAccessToTeam } from "../throwIfNotHaveAdminAccessToTeam"` points to packages/app-store/_utils/throwIfNotHaveAdminAccessToTeam.ts, a file that does not exist anywhere in the repo (base or head), breaking this module and every caller (hubspot, office365video, salesforce, stripepayment, tandemvideo, webex callback.ts) (confidence=100, severity=P0)

packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:96 — `await prisma.credential.update(...)` uses `prisma` but the file only imports `getAppKeysFromSlug` and `parseRefreshTokenResponse` from `_utils` plus various `@calcom/*` packages, with no `import prisma from "@calcom/prisma"` anywhere in the file, so `prisma` is an undefined identifier and this fails to compile (confidence=100, severity=P0)

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:94-101 — `const token = res?.data; googleCredentials.access_token = token.access_token; ...` treats the result of `refreshOAuthTokens` as always having a Google-style `.data` payload, but when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` is set, `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a raw fetch `Response` object which has no `.data` property, so `token` is `undefined` and `token.access_token` throws at runtime for exactly the new credential-sync path this PR implements (confidence=90, severity=P1)

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:97-101 — `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema); await prisma.credential.update({..., data: { key } })` stores the entire Zod `SafeParseReturnType` wrapper object (`{ success, data }`) as the credential's `key` instead of the parsed token fields (`key.data`), corrupting the stored google credential on every token refresh (confidence=85, severity=P0)

docs/tasks/task-001.md:1 — task doc was committed (d946f92) after all implementation work (b263064) with no prior stated intent, so the two-line task description was retrofitted to match already-completed work rather than the work being checked against a pre-existing accepted objective; this is not an objective-change-without-acceptance across iterations (there's only one implementation commit), but it means there is no genuine baseline intent to verify drift against (confidence=55, severity=P3)

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:97 — `parseRefreshTokenResponse()` returns the full zod `SafeParseReturnType` wrapper (`{success, data}`), but it is assigned straight to `key` and persisted via `prisma.credential.update({data:{key}})`, silently replacing every refreshed Google Calendar credential's `key` JSON with a malformed `{success,data}` blob instead of the flat token object the schema expects, permanently corrupting that row on the very next parse/refresh cycle (confidence=95, severity=P0).

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:25-27 — when a refresh response omits `refresh_token`, the helper substitutes the literal placeholder string `"refresh_token"` for the real value; in packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:263-271 this placeholder is spread over (and overwrites) the previously-valid `o365AuthCredentials.refresh_token` before being written back with `prisma.credential.update`, so any refresh cycle where Microsoft doesn't return a fresh refresh_token silently destroys the stored real token, requiring the user to fully re-authenticate (confidence=80, severity=P0).

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:31 — `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body)` uses `.parse` not `.safeParse`, so a malformed webhook body throws an uncaught ZodError inside the handler and the client receives a raw 500 instead of a 400 (confidence=85, severity=P2)

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:57 — `symmetricDecrypt(...)` followed by `JSON.parse(...)` throws uncaught if the ciphertext is malformed or `CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY` is wrong/empty, producing a raw unhandled 500 rather than a controlled error response (confidence=80, severity=P2)

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8 — the credential-sync `fetch` call has no timeout/AbortController, so a hung `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` blocks the entire token-refresh chain (and any calendar operation awaiting it) indefinitely (confidence=85, severity=P2)

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:15 — the sync-path response is returned to callers without checking `response.ok`/status, and packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:94 destructures `res?.data` straight from that raw fetch Response (which has no `.data` field), so `token` is undefined and the resulting TypeError is swallowed by the outer catch (googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:103-108), silently returning the old, potentially expired `myGoogleAuth` as if refresh succeeded (confidence=75, severity=P1)

packages/app-store/hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts:177 — when the sync path is active, `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a raw, unvalidated fetch Response cast to `HubspotToken`; `hubspotRefreshToken.expiresIn` is undefined so `expiryDate` becomes `NaN` and `accessToken` is undefined, yet this is written to `prisma.credential.update` (line 193) and `hubspotClient.setAccessToken(undefined)` is called with no thrown error, silently persisting a corrupted credential as if the refresh succeeded (confidence=75, severity=P1)

packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:86 — `if (response.statusText !== "OK")` is an unreliable HTTP-failure check because `statusText` is not guaranteed to be the literal string "OK" across runtimes/proxies (e.g. undici can return an empty statusText), so this can either let a non-2xx response through unflagged or reject a valid 200 (confidence=55, severity=P2)

packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:92 — the `if (!accessTokenParsed.success) return Promise.reject(...)` branch is unreachable dead code because `parseRefreshTokenResponse` (packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:21-23) already throws `Error("Invalid refreshed tokens were returned")` before returning when parsing fails, so this caller-side check can never observe `success === false`, masking that the callee's own throw path is what actually runs and is untested here (confidence=85, severity=P3)

packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:263 — replacing the previous `console.error` (which logged the specific zodError and raw MS response body) with `parseRefreshTokenResponse` regresses diagnostics: on parse failure only a generic `Error("Invalid refreshed tokens were returned")` is thrown with no detail about which fields were invalid or what Microsoft actually returned, making failed office365 token refreshes harder to debug in production (confidence=80, severity=P2)

packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/api/add.ts:17 — unrelated drive-by change hardcodes `zoho-bigin` in place of `appConfig.slug` in the redirect URI, unexplained and untraceable to the "OAuth credential sync" task, and reintroduces a config/slug drift risk if the app is ever renamed or forked (confidence=75, severity=P2)

packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/api/add.ts:17 — this single-line diff sits inside an otherwise pure import-path-relocation file, so it should have been split into its own commit/PR rather than bundled with the oauth-utils move, making the change harder to review or revert independently (confidence=60, severity=P3)

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:24-29 — if CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET is entirely unset in the process environment (undefined, not the empty-string default from .env.example), `req.headers[headerName]` for a request that omits the header is also `undefined`, so `undefined !== undefined` is `false` and the secret check is bypassed entirely, letting any unauthenticated caller create/overwrite OAuth credentials for any userId (confidence=90, severity=P1)

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:31-91 — the webhook trusts a single static shared secret to authorize writes to an attacker-chosen `userId` in the request body with no per-user scoping/signature, so leaking or brute-forcing one CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET grants an attacker write access to overwrite OAuth credentials for every user in the instance (confidence=100, severity=P1)

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:25-26 — the webhook secret is compared with `!==`, a non-constant-time string comparison, allowing a timing side-channel attack to incrementally recover CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET over many requests (confidence=75, severity=P2)

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:58 — `process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY || ""` silently falls back to an empty-string encryption key when the env var is unset, producing a publicly-known/predictable key so anyone can forge the `keys` ciphertext accepted by symmetricDecrypt instead of the operation failing closed (confidence=70, severity=P2)

goldens.comment: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.

The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.

When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the fetch Response, but several callers (for example GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting res.data, and HubspotCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting a HubspotToken) assume it returns the integration-specific token object. That mismatch will cause runtime errors in the sync-enabled path unless the return type or those call sites are adjusted.

When the sync endpoint path is used, res is a fetch Response and has no .data; res?.data will be undefined and token.access_token will throw at runtime. This relies on a consistent return shape from refreshOAuthTokens, which isn’t guaranteed currently.

The `refreshOAuthTokens` function is passed `credentialId` instead of `userId`, which breaks the credential sync functionality by causing incorrect user lookups. This issue can lead to failures in syncing user credentials, impacting user experience.

The Salesforce integration checks `response.statusText` instead of `response.ok` when handling OAuth token refresh responses. This can lead to unreliable behavior, as a successful response may not be correctly identified, resulting in the use of stale credentials and potential authentication failures.

The `jsforce.Connection` is created using stale `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url` after a token refresh, which can lead to authentication failures and incorrect data access. Ensure that the connection is established using the refreshed token values instead.

The `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` function can throw on invalid payloads, resulting in 500 Internal Server Errors instead of the expected 400 Bad Request responses. This can lead to confusion for clients and hinder proper error handling.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:62-92 — findFirst-then-create has no DB unique constraint on (userId, appId) backing it, so two concurrent webhook deliveries for the same user+app both miss the findFirst and both insert, producing duplicate Credential rows for the same app (confidence=75, severity=P1)

adjudication.rationale: The new webhook handler does a non-atomic `findFirst` on `{ userId, appId }` and then either `update` or `create` (apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts: findFirst → create/update). This pattern is vulnerable to a race where two concurrent requests can both miss the `findFirst` and both attempt `create`, causing duplicates *unless* a DB-level unique constraint exists. The diff does not include the Prisma schema/migrations, so the claim that there is definitively “no DB unique constraint” cannot be verified from the provided changes, but the code as written still introduces a concurrency risk if such a constraint is absent.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:83-90 — credential is created with raw userId ownership and no team/org scoping check, an architectural mismatch with packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/createOAuthAppCredential.ts in the same diff which explicitly models team-owned credentials (teamId, throwIfNotHaveAdminAccessToTeam); the webhook path bypasses that ownership model entirely and only trusts appSlug->app existence, not user eligibility for the app (confidence=70, severity=P2)

adjudication.rationale: The new webhook handler (`apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`) only accepts `userId` in its request schema and creates/updates credentials by `where: { userId, appId: appMetadata.slug }`, then `prisma.credential.create({ data: { key, userId, appId, type } })` with no possibility of `teamId`/org scoping or any eligibility/authorization check beyond “user exists”, “app exists”, and matching webhook secret. In the same diff, the OAuth credential creation utility (`packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/createOAuthAppCredential.ts`) explicitly supports team-owned credentials and performs an admin-access check (`throwIfNotHaveAdminAccessToTeam`). This is a concrete architectural inconsistency introduced by the webhook path, but the diff alone doesn’t prove it is an outright defect (it may be intentionally user-scoped for self-host credential sync).

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:24-29 — if CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET is entirely unset in the process environment (undefined, not the empty-string default from .env.example), `req.headers[headerName]` for a request that omits the header is also `undefined`, so `undefined !== undefined` is `false` and the secret check is bypassed entirely, letting any unauthenticated caller create/overwrite OAuth credentials for any userId (confidence=90, severity=P1)

adjudication.rationale: The handler first blocks all requests unless `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` is truthy (`if (!APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED) return 403`). In `packages/lib/constants.ts`, `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` is defined as `process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET && process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY`, so if `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` is unset/undefined (or even set to an empty string), the endpoint returns 403 before reaching the webhook-secret header comparison. Therefore the described bypass (undefined header vs undefined secret) is not reachable from the diff’s logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:31-91 — the webhook trusts a single static shared secret to authorize writes to an attacker-chosen `userId` in the request body with no per-user scoping/signature, so leaking or brute-forcing one CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET grants an attacker write access to overwrite OAuth credentials for every user in the instance (confidence=100, severity=P1)

adjudication.rationale: The newly added API route `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts` authorizes credential creation/updates solely by checking a single header value against `process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` (lines ~15-27) and then accepts an attacker-controlled `userId` from the parsed body (zod schema + `prisma.user.findUnique({ id: reqBody.userId })`). There is no additional scoping (e.g., per-user secret, signed payload, or server-to-server identity) before performing `prisma.credential.update/create` for that `userId` and `appSlug`. Therefore, compromise/guessing of the one shared secret would allow overwriting OAuth credential keys for any user in the instance, matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:25-26 — the webhook secret is compared with `!==`, a non-constant-time string comparison, allowing a timing side-channel attack to incrementally recover CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET over many requests (confidence=75, severity=P2)

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added API route `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the webhook secret is validated via a direct inequality check: `req.headers[...] !== process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` (around lines 25–26 in the new file). This is a normal JS string comparison and not a constant-time comparison, which can theoretically leak information via timing differences when repeatedly probing the endpoint. The diff shows no constant-time comparison helper (e.g., `crypto.timingSafeEqual`) being used here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:58 — `process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY || ""` silently falls back to an empty-string encryption key when the env var is unset, producing a publicly-known/predictable key so anyone can forge the `keys` ciphertext accepted by symmetricDecrypt instead of the operation failing closed (confidence=70, severity=P2)

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the decrypt line uses `process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY || ""`, but the handler first checks `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` and returns 403 if false. `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` (added in `packages/lib/constants.ts`) is only truthy when both `process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` and `process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY` are set, so the decrypt path is not reachable when the encryption key env var is unset. Therefore the claimed “empty-string encryption key” acceptance/forgery scenario is not verifiable from this diff.
